property_summary: Calling owner() on a Clone contract always returns the address of the creator (owner) passed at offset 0x0, but the buggy version returns the collateral address at offset 0x14, so for any Clone deployed with different owner and collateral addresses, the return values differ.

For any Clone instance deployed via ClonesWithImmutableArgs, calling owner() returns the original owner address packed at immutable arg offset 0x0, but the buggy version returns the collateral address at offset 0x14 instead, so the outputs differ whenever owner and collateral are distinct.

For any valid clone deployment, owner() must return the original creator address (offset 0x0), not the debt token address (offset 0x28). The bug changes the offset so owner() returns the debt address, violating this invariant.
For every clone created by the factory, the owner() getter must return the original factory-injected owner address, not the debt token address; the bug makes owner() return the debt token address.

For any clone created by the factory via generateCooler, the owner() getter must return the msg.sender passed to generateCooler, not the debt token address; the bug changes the offset to 0x28 causing owner() to return the debt token address instead.

For any properly constructed Clone, calldata at offset 0x0 (which stores the owner) must differ from calldata at offset 0x28 (which stores the debt token) when the factory-injected addresses are distinct; the bug makes owner() return the debt token address, thus when a factory generates a cooler with distinct owner and debt token, the buggy owner() equals debt().
For any cloned cooler with distinct owner and debt token addresses, the reference owner() equals the factory-injected owner, while the buggy owner() incorrectly equals the debt token address.

The owner() function must always return the address of the initial owner, not the factory address; the bug makes owner() return the factory address instead, violating the invariant that owner() returns the original deployer's address.
owner() must return the initial immutable-args-derived owner address and not the factory address; the bug makes owner() equal to the factory address.

The owner() function must return the original deployer address (immutable arg at offset 0x0), not the factory address (immutable arg at offset 0x3c); the bug swaps them making owner() equal factory().

For any Clone contract instance created by CoolerFactory, owner() must return the original deployer address (the factory caller), not the factory address itself; the bug replaces the offset making owner() return factory(), which is different from the actual deployer.

owner() must return the address stored at immutable args offset 0x0, which is set by the factory to msg.sender (the caller of generateCooler), and must not equal factory(); the bug changes the offset to 0x3c, making owner() return the factory address, violating the invariant that owner() != factory().

The owner address returned by C.owner() must match the address stored in the first 20 bytes of calldata after the immutable args offset; the buggy version returns a value based on a full 32-byte read, causing a mismatch when those upper 12 bytes are non-zero.

The owner() function must return the address correctly extracted from the first 20 bytes (0x0 offset) of the calldata, not an address derived from a full 32-byte read; the buggy version casts a uint256, so when the twelfth byte of the address is non-zero, the high 12 bytes of the uint256 are non-zero and the cast to address truncates them, yielding a different address.

For any clone contract created via ClonesWithImmutableArgs, the owner address returned by owner() must equal the first 20 bytes of calldata at the immutable args offset; the buggy version reads a full 32-byte word and truncates, so when any of the upper 12 bytes of that word (bytes 20-31 after the offset) are non-zero, the returned address differs.

For any clone created with valid immutable args, owner() must return the address formed by the first 20 bytes of calldata after the derived offset; the buggy version casts a full 32-byte uint256 to address, returning an incorrect value whenever any of the upper 12 bytes of that word are non-zero.

For any clone created with ClonesWithImmutableArgs, the address returned by owner() must equal the first 20 bytes of calldata at the immutable args offset; the mutant reads a full 32-byte uint256 before casting, so when any upper 12 bytes of that word are non-zero, the truncated address differs from the real owner.

Calling collateral() on the reference C always returns the address of the collateral token derived from immutable args, whereas the mutant returns the zero address; therefore, for any correctly deployed C, the returned ERC20 address must have non-zero code length, which the mutant violates for some deployment.

For any C instance created by the factory, the return of collateral() must equal the address of the collateral token used at creation, which is never the zero address; the mutant returns address(0), violating this invariant.
Calling collateral() on the reference C always returns an address with non-zero code size (a deployed ERC20), whereas the mutant returns the zero address, which has zero code size.

For any loan request cleared on a correctly deployed C instance, the collateral token address returned by collateral() must equal the collateral address emitted in the ClearRequest event by the factory; the mutant returns address(0), which will never match the address of the transferred collateral token.

For any C instance created via the factory's clone with immutable args, the address returned by collateral() must equal the ERC20 address encoded in the immutable args at offset 0x14; the mutant returns address(0), which differs for all valid deployments.
A call to collateral() must return the ERC20 at the immutable arg offset 0x14 (the collateral token), not the owner address at offset 0x0.
For any deployed clone, calling collateral() returns the address encoded at immutable arg offset 0x14, which is always different from the owner address at offset 0x0.
For any clone deployed by the factory, calling collateral() returns the address of the collateral token, which must match the token the factory used as collateral for that cooler.

For any clone deployed through the factory's generateCooler, calling collateral() must return the same address as the collateral ERC20 token used when the cooler was created, but the mutant returns the owner address instead.

For any clone deployed by the factory through generateCooler, calling collateral() must return the same address as the collateral ERC20 argument passed to the factory, but the mutant returns the owner address instead.
The collateral() function must always return the collateral token address (at offset 0x14) as configured during deployment, but the mutant returns the debt token address (at offset 0x28) instead.

The return value of collateral() must equal the collateral token address stored at immutable offset 0x14, but the mutant returns the debt token address at offset 0x28, causing inequality with the expected collateral token when the two tokens differ.
